sanity_expectations: finite and real over the whole Lt range
C increases with Lt then approaches a finite asymptote (no blow-up)
specific-binding contribution rises monotonically toward the Rt~1 plateau (near full receptor occupancy)
nonspecific saturable contribution is bounded above by Bmax~1
total C is bounded, roughly <= Rt + Bmax ~ 2
child C stays at or below parent C at large Lt because the nonspecific term saturates rather than growing linearly
excitation_report: sigma=0.02, k=5. Two additive terms: (1) nonspecific saturable Langmuir term rms=0.609 -> 30.4x sigma; (2) specific quadratic-binding/Hill term rms=0.972 -> 48.6x sigma. NEW term (child minus parent = saturation of nonspecific binding at Bmax) max effect 1.786 -> 89.3x sigma, strongest at Lt~10.0 (the peak of N(Lt)). All terms >> 5*sigma; auto_balance converged with no coefficient changes needed.
role_corrections: C: O->O (confirmed: LHS, explicitly solvable for target)
Lt: V->V (confirmed: total-ligand sweep axis, gets sampling range)
Rt: P->P (confirmed: total receptor conc, fixed)
Lsat: P->P (confirmed: nonspecific half-attenuation scale, fixed)
Bmax: P->P (confirmed: nonspecific saturation capacity, fixed; new parameter of this step)
rationale: Static explicit binding relation C = f(Lt; params); analyze_expression shows no derivatives/integrals and explicit solvability, so equation_type=explicit -> evaluate_explicit. Lt is the only sampling axis (total-ligand sweep, 0.01-50 spans the rise-to-saturation of both the specific Hill/quadratic term and the nonspecific peak at Lt=Lsat=10). All other symbols are fixed constants at physiologically sensible magnitudes (tight-binding Kd<Rt, nH=1, nonspecific peak N~2.5 comparable to Bmax=1 so the new saturation term bites). The new term relative to the parent is the Bmax saturation of nonspecific binding; it peaks at 89x sigma near Lt~10, so it is strongly visible above the injected noise.

new_term.delta_expr: evaluated numerically as current expression minus parent

scenario_text: A tight-binding ligand is mixed with a receptor at a fixed total receptor concentration, and the complex is allowed to reach equilibrium. As total ligand is increased, the amount of bound complex rises and saturates near full receptor occupancy. Bound complex is measured across a total-ligand sweep. The task is to recover the equilibrium bound fraction as a function of total ligand.
